analysis.title: GS Kamshad - GS TMT TODAY 11.9.26
key_insights: Futures are bid ahead of Monday's open (Nasdaq +50bps, S&P +60bps, Russell +125bps) after a week of violent post-Election rotation, large cuts in gross and net exposure, and a large cut in Tech length. WTI is -3.5% on hopes for Iran de-escalation after Trump said extensive strikes are 'highly unlikely', conditional on Iran signing 'a very strong agreement'.

NVDA is -5% pre-market after its board launched an independent investigation following Bloomberg headlines about CEO Jensen Huang. Hyperscalers are bid (AMZN +3%, META +3%, GOOGL +2%, MSFT +2%) while levered datacenter names are down 2-5% (CRWV, IREN, NBIS).

Info Tech was by far the most dollar net sold global and US sector last week. The percentage of selling in global Info Tech was about on par with the largest net-selling weeks on GS record (since 2016). US Info Tech net allocation is 14.4% of US net market value, in the 1st/1st/3rd percentiles on 1-year/3-year/5-year lookbacks.

GS Semis (Schneider) says the market faces two tensions: how the funding gap between hyperscaler and AI lab capex and free cash flow gets closed, and whether enough land, power and shell is coming online to match Street semi estimates. After the Nov. 3 election, uncertainty over datacenter build pace in states such as Texas pushed the second tension forward. SOX is down 13% in the past week and 31% since Oct. 1. GS views stocks as oversold and sees compelling risk/reward in select names, though there may be few catalysts before year end.

GS NVDA 3Q preview (Schneider): expects strong results and guidance and near-term fundamentals ahead of Street estimates. Investor focus will be power/shell visibility through 2028, sustainability of AI infrastructure funding, and AI demand health including agentic-driven CPU upside. Stock trades at about 11x GS CY27 EPS estimate of $16.70. Buy reiterated, with near-term challenges until visibility improves.

Callahan: NDX fell about 5% last week and is on a 4-week losing streak. SOX is -28% over 22 days, one of its largest rolling 1-month drawdowns on record. The week had record put volumes, elevated ETF volumes, signs of panic in vol metrics, elevated sell skews and oversold conditions, which could set up technical relief as vol normalizes. Investor conversations began shifting to what is priced in for capex/GW builds, mostly a 2028+ question rather than 2027.

Prime Services: S&P 500 fell 2.7% on the week. Goldminers, ACA beneficiaries and homebuilders outperformed. Memory, optical networks and oil had the largest losses. US equities were modestly net sold, with the largest single-stock net selling in 4 months partly offset by buying in macro products. HFs sold US Industrials at the fastest pace since April 2020.

Prime shares color: Friday's market bounce had semis up about 3.5%, which felt healthy rather than a beta squeeze. Long-only funds were moderate net sellers (steady semis supply) and HFs were net buyers, driven by a cover bid in macro expressions on Friday.

Systematic/CTA signals are negative in about 60% of global equity markets at short and medium-term horizons, including the S&P. GS expects CTAs to sell $28bn of SPX futures over the next week and $45bn over the next month in the baseline scenario, taking the position to net short. S&P short and medium-term trigger levels are about 7685 and 7550.

Derivatives: Thursday saw an extreme vol repricing. Clients had taken off protection into Wednesday's post-midterm relief rally, leaving the market underhedged. GS vol panic index hit 9.57 out of 10, the 3rd largest daily jump ever after the 4th largest drop on Wednesday. The combined two-day swing was the largest on record.

ETFs: Thursday was the third largest notional volume day in the GS dataset for US-listed ETFs at $580bn, 33% of the tape (28% average). Friday morning ETF share was 36% of the tape with dollar volumes +65% vs the 20-day average.

Basket idea: GS likes shorting its Diversified Staples Basket (GSXUSTAP). Earnings and dividend yields are unattractive relative to fixed income, growth is insufficient, revisions are rolling over, and valuations are in the 90th percentile vs the last year. The basket outperformed SPX by nearly 20% in the last month. Staples have historically lagged over 3 months after similar events except late 2021/early 2022.

TMT specialists (Callahan and Joseph): Semiconductor valuations are nearly 50% off the highs, and the question is whether the skew has over-priced a slowdown. The path higher for Tech depends on earnings (NVDA still to come), financing visibility, oil and rates relief, lowered expectations and reset positioning.

Oracle (ORCL) investor meetings 11/4-11/6 with CEO, CFO and IR: Oracle says it operates data centers on 'extreme agility' (flexible architecture, contracting models, capacity stand-up). It knows how much each contracting model (vendor financing, customer prepayment, BYOH) contributes to backlog, has stress-tested downside scenarios, and says no more capital is needed this cycle after completing a $20bn debt/equity raise last week. It sees minimal risk to the 7GW planned online through May 2028, as all is contracted and under construction. GS expects new builds to shift internationally.
Apple: per Bloomberg, new CEO Ternus pressed software chief Craig Federighi to be more ambitious on AI and move beyond Siri improvements toward an autonomous agent.

China internet 3Q preview: GS expects a mixed top-line, with soft consumption weighing on eCommerce, ads and local services, while Games (most preferred sub-sector), Cloud and Internet verticals are more defensive. The 4Q outlook is the key watch, with weak eCommerce GMV growth since October. GS expects sequentially lower AI capex into the Dec and Mar quarters from tight chip supply but higher 2027-28E capex on higher compute prices and domestic capacity ramp. Aggregate China internet net profit is forecast +9% y/y in Sep quarter vs -10% and -32% in the Jun and Mar quarters.

Week ahead: S&P implied move through Friday is 2.29%. CPI is Tuesday (GS at +16bps for core m/m, est +0.3%) with a slate of Fed speakers. Neocloud earnings: CRWV (Tuesday) and NBIS (Thursday). Other dates include PPI Friday and jobless claims Thursday.
